emailSubject: FMB News | Malacañang Assures Q2 GDP Slowdown Is Temporary | August 8, 2026 | 6:00 AM PHT
headline: Philippine Economy Grows 2.3% in Q2 as Construction Slumps
deck: The Philippine economy expanded 2.3% year on year in the second quarter of 2026, its slowest annual pace since 2021, as construction and investment contracted.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Philippine economy grew 2.3% from a year earlier in the second quarter of 2026, slowing from 2.8% in the first quarter and falling below the 2.8% median forecast in a Reuters poll.
The result was the country's weakest annual growth rate since 2021. Growth for the first half of 2026 stood at 2.6%.

sections.heading: What we know
paragraphs: Construction contracted 14.8% from a year earlier during the quarter. Investment declined 9.2%, its fourth consecutive quarterly contraction, while household spending growth eased to 2.8% from 3.0% in the first quarter.

The government's revised full-year growth target is 3.5% to 4.5%. The 2.6% first-half result was below the lower end of that range. Inflation averaged 5.0% during the first seven months of 2026, limiting household purchasing power.

sections.heading: Government response
paragraphs: Economic Planning Secretary Arsenio Balisacan said the weak result required decisive action while pointing to early signs that activity could improve in the second half. The government expects infrastructure spending to increase as recently approved projects begin.
The available evidence supports cautious optimism about a possible recovery, but it does not guarantee that the slowdown will be temporary or that the full-year target will be reached.

sections.heading: Background
paragraphs: The economy grew 5.5% in the second quarter of 2025, according to the Philippine Statistics Authority. Growth then slowed substantially, reaching 2.8% in the first quarter of 2026 before easing further in the second quarter.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: Slower growth can mean weaker demand for workers, delayed business expansion, and less momentum for wage and income gains. The contraction in construction also matters because public and private projects support employment, transport, housing, and local supply chains.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: The pace at which delayed or newly approved infrastructure projects can begin is still uncertain. It also remains to be seen whether household spending will recover while inflation stays above the government's target.

sections.heading: What happens next
paragraphs: The government will monitor project implementation and second-half activity. The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas is scheduled to review monetary policy on August 27, when it will weigh weak growth against elevated inflation.
